question: Rods and cone cells are found in:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Eyes**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rods and cone cells** are specialized photoreceptor cells found in the **retina of the eyes**.
 
• **Rods** are responsible for vision at low light levels (scotopic vision) and do not mediate color vision.
 
• **Cones** are active at higher light levels (photopic vision), are capable of color vision, and are responsible for high spatial acuity.
 
• The human retina contains approximately 120 million rod cells and 6 million cone cells.
 
• Rods and cones are essential for converting light into electrical signals, which are then processed by the brain to produce visual images.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **eye** is a complex organ composed of various parts including the cornea, lens, retina, and optic nerve.
 
• The **retina** is the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye that contains the photoreceptor cells (rods and cones).
 
• The **optic nerve** transmits visual information from the retina to the brain.
 
• Common eye conditions involving rods and cones include **retinitis pigmentosa** and **color blindness**.
 
• Regular eye check-ups are important for maintaining good visual health and early detection of potential issues.
